public_rationale: Primary research revised on September 25 explicitly identifies hallucination as unresolved. OpenAI's deployment disclosure also reports factual fabrication in GPT-4V. Together they support the ordinary claim that the problem persisted near the post date. Neither source requires the stronger conclusion that most answers were false or that no progress had occurred.
limitations: The research was a preprint at publication.
The deployment evidence is company-reported and includes image-based tasks.
This assessment does not establish how common hallucinations were across all user requests.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: LLMs have not solved the hallucination problem.

statement.excerpt: Rumors that LLMs have solved then hallucination problem are greatly exaggerated.

our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is that factual fabrication remained an unresolved limitation of contemporary LLMs. This does not claim that every model or answer hallucinates, or that improvements had stopped.
The context illustrates the present with examples from last week and last night. I use the last complete calendar week before publication through the post date: September 25–October 4, 2023.

A contemporary research assessment or deployment disclosure identifying continuing factual fabrication can establish that the problem remained unsolved. It need not measure the frequency of all user encounters.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporary primary research or deployment evidence identifies factual fabrication as a continuing material limitation of leading LLMs.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Contemporary evidence establishes that factual fabrication had effectively been eliminated across ordinary factual tasks in leading LLMs, with the alleged continuing failures disproved or confined to superseded systems.

evidence.explanation: The revised paper identifies hallucination as an unresolved contemporary problem and reports experiments reducing it through verification. The event date identifies this current-state assessment, not the undisclosed dates of individual experimental runs.
OpenAI reports factual fabrication as a limitation of the model being deployed in late September. This dates the disclosed deployment limitation, not the earlier red-team sessions.
